statements.impact_statement: The Marvin attack is a timing sidechannel in RSA decryption and signing, which leaks PRIVATE-key operations. The `rsa` crate reaches this graph only through `pgp` 0.20, which the instrument uses to VERIFY detached OpenPGP signatures on version content (RM common master06 §Digital Signature): a verification-only path over public keys. The instrument holds no RSA private key and performs no RSA decryption or signing, so there is no secret for the sidechannel to leak. No fixed release exists upstream; the deleting event is the rsa 0.10 release, taken the day it ships (deny.toml carries the same adjudication as the gate).

The advisory reports timing variability in `crypto-bigint` operations meant to be constant-time, which leaks SECRET integers. `crypto-bigint` 0.5.5 reaches this graph only through `pgp` 0.20's `elliptic-curve` 0.13 stack (ecdsa, p256, p384, p521, k256) and `cx448`, and `pgp` 0.21 still requires `elliptic-curve` ^0.13. The signature judge verifies detached OpenPGP signatures over PUBLIC keys only, and nothing in the instrument signs with OpenPGP or holds an OpenPGP secret key (#593 removed the run-record signer), so no secret scalar is ever decoded through that stack. Deleting event: a `pgp` release on `elliptic-curve` 0.14 / `crypto-bigint` 0.7.6 or later, or `pgp` leaving the graph (deny.toml carries the same adjudication as the gate).
